messages.subject: Re: problem installing rJava on x86_64
messages.body_plain:
Andy,

On Oct 4, 2006, at 4:53 PM, Liaw, Andy wrote:

> Hi everyone,
>
> I'm trying to get JGR up and running on our Opteron box with a  
> freshly built R-2.4.0, but got the error shown below.  (Sorry, it's  
> rather long.)  Can anyone shed some light on this?
>

First off - some people reported that  Sun's Java 1.5 is broken on  
x86_64 and recommend 1.6 beta which is much better, so your mileage  
may vary. Having said that, you seem to have also compiler issues:

It appears that your PGI compiler doesn't support variadic macros:

> PGC-S-0224-Syntax error in #define, formal ... not identifier  
> (Rglue.c: 23)
> PGC-S-0224-Syntax error in #define, formal ... not identifier  
> (Rglue.c: 54)

Maybe you need some compiler-specific flag to enable the support (vms  
are defined in C99 standard). If in doubt, I'd recommend using gcc  
(at least as pp) instead (which is known to work). Another solution  
is to replace both definitions by void foo(char *fmt, ...) {}; but  
that will bloat the code (as the arguments still have to be processed).

FWIW: Just in case you wanted to use JRI (which is an optional part  
of rJava and required to run JGR), note that your R is missing libR.so:

> checking whether JRI should be compiled (autodetect)... no

If you want to enable this, you'll need to compile R with --enable-R- 
shlib.

Cheers,
Simon

pwdfile authentication fails with the message "Rserve exception: login
failed, request status: authorization failed".

messages.subject: RE: problem installing rJava on x86_64
messages.body_plain:
Just to report back to the list:

Thanks very much to Simon's help, I was able to get rJava working by:

- Use the updated version (0.4-11) that Simon provided that removed
  the use of vms.

- Install jdk 1.6.0 beta 2 for x86_64 (1.5.0_08 for x86_64 has 
  known problems).

Now I got rJava working, as well as JavaGD.  However, I'm stuck 
with JGR.  It installs fine, but when I try to run it, it gives
me a mysterious stack overflow, and lately with a JVM segfault.
Don't know if it's problem with the PGI (6.2) compilers, or the 
jdk 1.6.0 beta 2, or some combination of both...

Cheers,
Andy

> What is the current state of affairs about JGR and R 2.4.0.

R should have no effect on the usability of JGR.

Cheers,
